articleTitle: microConceptBERT: Concept-Relation Based Document Information Extraction Framework
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Extracting information from documents is a crucial task in natural language processing research. Existing information extraction methodologies often focus on specific domains, such as medicine, education or finance, and are limited by language constraints. However, more comprehensive approaches that transcend document types, languages, contexts, and structures would significantly advance the field proposed in recent research. This study addresses this challenge by introducing microConceptBERT: a concept-relations-based framework for document information extraction, which offers flexibility for various document processing tasks while accounting for hierarchical, semantic, and heuristic features. The proposed framework has been applied to a question-answering task on benchmark datasets: SQUAD 2.0 and DOCVQA. Notably, the F1 evaluation metric attains an outperforming 87.01 performance rate on the SQUAD 2.0 dataset compared to baseline models: BERT-base and BERT-large models.

articleTitle: AI-Based Covid-19 Diagnosis Approach Using Chest X-Ray and Chest CT-Images
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The spread rate of the novel Covid-19 has been exponential since December 2019. The shortage of Covid-19 PCR testing kits is worsened by the lengthy turnaround process for test results that has a high rate of false negatives roughly above 30-40%. Among the available approaches for Covid-19 detection, AI-driven approaches are popular, but limited to identifying the patients based on one type of data either CT scan or Chest X-Ray images. Following research work is proposing an Artificial Intelligence-based Covid-19 detection application that can simultaneously analyze the images generated from CT scans and Chest X-Rays to improve the accurate results in real-time identifying Covid-19 infected patients with the use of Transfer Learning.

articleTitle: RSSI and Machine Learning-Based Indoor Localization Systems for Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Widespread use of the Internet of Things (IoT) is being made in a number of application areas to save costs and improve performance. These types of applications also include services that are dependent on localization. When a sensor node is localized, an IoT network may use that information to identify it. A Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI), which gauges the intensity of the signal received from the sensor nodes, is typically used in conjunction with supervised Machine Learning (ML) algorithms in localization methods. In this study, a unique indoor and outdoor localization and navigation technique is presented that makes use of LoRA nodes and a highly accurate machine learning model. The suggested method has cutting-edge features and shows considerable gains in accuracy and dependability. These discoveries offer potential answers for practical applications and boost localization technology.

articleTitle: Automated Evaluation of Student Answers for Geometric Questions Based on the Theorem 'Angles on a Straight Line Add to 180±’
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Evaluation of the answers for a geometry-related question is a much more challenging task due to the usage of multiple methods for solving this kind of problem. However, in this research, an automated system to evaluate the students' answers to geometric questions has been introduced. The image of the problem and the image of the student's answer are the inputs of this system. The system can evaluate student's answers by using the identified angles and creating equations in the system. Furthermore, the system allocates the marks for correct steps and provides feedback on whether the answer is correct or incorrect. Here, the set of rules using “sympy” has been used to create the solved answer by the system. Currently, the system evaluates the answers only for the problems related to the theorem” Angles on a Straight Line Add to 180°”. The system has been tested with 30 student answers for 10 questions. 18 were correct out of these 30 answers.

articleTitle: Enhancing Visual Fidelity in Unpaired Night-to-Day Image Translation through a Perceptual Quality Focused Training Objective
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Nighttime driving poses visibility challenges, but image translation methods can help by transforming night images into day-like scenes. The Cycle-GAN is a versatile unpaired image translation model which can easily be adept to night-to-day image translation tasks. However, it generates unnatural and unrealistic outcomes in these cases. This study is focused on addressing this with a novel training strategy for the Cycle-GAN, employing a tailored training objective that incorporates perceptual quality optimization. This training objective aims to boost the naturalness and perceptual quality of the generated images by preserving high-level image features. The optimization process involves minimizing Euclidean distances between synthesized and target image feature maps, which are derived from the pre-trained VGG19 network. Experimental findings attest to the effectiveness of this method, revealing noteworthy improvements of 8% in Inception Score, 2% in NIQE Score, and 13% in BRISQUE Score.

articleTitle: Sign Language Translation Techniques Using Artificial Intelligence for the Hearing Impaired Community in Sri Lanka: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Hearing Impaired individuals routinely encounter limitations in their involvement in social interactions, access to intriguing information, and participation in everyday activities, among various other aspects. However, the hardest part of their interactions with regular people is communication, because sign language is the primary language of those who are hearing impaired. However, the general public is unaware of sign language. Each country has its own sign language. However, there are some striking similarities between them. In Sri Lanka, hearing impaired people use Sri Lankan Sign Language (SLSL) as their communication language. There is several research done on Sign Language recognition and translation. But no fully functioning system is utilized for Sri Lankan Sign Language translation. To find the gap in this area, we conducted a systematic literature review using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) method that analyses 12 studies on Sign Language Translation (SLT). As per the literature review, Image Processing (IP) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are the most used techniques for Sign Language translation. But these methods have limitations: not enough data, differences in how people use sign language, difficulty in translating in real-time, not capturing cultural aspects, needing specific equipment, and understanding the context of conversations. Recognizing and solving these problems is important, especially for languages like SLSL. Future research should focus on getting more data, making translation work for different cultures, and improving real-time translation. This will help hearing impaired people communicate better with others.

articleTitle: ECG Beat Classification using Capsule Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) is a low-cost, non-invasive technology used to detect cardiac activity which leads to the detection of diseases related to the cardiovascular system. Due to the substantial volume of data generated in long-term ECG monitoring, the classification of ECG beats and reaching a justifiable diagnosis have been tedious tasks. Despite many machine learning solutions being provided for ECG classification, no study has specifically used the relationships between ECG waveform features as the basis for modeling such solutions and extracting the explanations based on those features. Therefore, based on this concept, a capsule network solution was developed for the classification of ECG beats. The improved accuracy in this classification consequently extended the solution to produce feature-wise explanations as well. The evaluation showed an overall 97.94% accuracy in beat classification. The accuracy for normal, left and right bundle branch block, atrial and ventricular beat classification yielded 98.89%, 99.44%, 99.56%, 98.83% and 99.17% respectively. For each of these classifications, feature-wise explanations were also generated. Hence it was concluded that this approach, based on capsule networks to classify ECG beats has recorded a higher accuracy than the existing approaches with feature-wise explanations leading to better diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Model for Enhancing User Experience in an E-learning System: A Review on Student Behavior and Content Formatting
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: With the propagation of E-learning platforms, monitoring and evaluating student performance and providing targeted content to enhance student learning capabilities is a major concern. This review will mainly focus on student behavior extraction and content formatting in relation to E-learning platforms. The usage of different data mining techniques to extract user interactions with E-learning platforms and identify patterns of interest have also been reviewed. The targeted recommendation of content can be done to each individual student. The review will be open to the path for manipulating content such that the interest of the target individuals remains high, due to the use of content translations and formatting across multiple media. There are some highlights of both student behavior extraction and content formatting. In student behavior extraction, person-alized learning, increased satisfaction, and early intervention could be achieved. The content formatting of an E-learning management system should be added headings to indicate the main topics of the paragraph, break up the text into shorter paragraphs to make it easier to read, add images to illustrate key concepts, and use a consistent style throughout the paragraph. Finally, these extracted concepts can be formed into a model and then we present a model taking into account student behavior and content formatting aspects. This model is formed based on the review. The model can be used to deal with intelligent E-learning systems where the system will be able to identify the student behaviors and then accordingly the content formatting.

articleTitle: Impact of Personal Intelligent Agent's Anthropomorphism on Gen-Z Consumers' Intention in the Retail Sector
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: A personal intelligent agent (PIA) is a device that uses natural language to help a person act in an intelligent way. Siri and Alexa are two examples. These agents are powerful computer programs that can work on their own and be proactive. They can also learn and adapt to change, respond to their surroundings, finish tasks in a good amount of time, and talk to the user using natural language to understand directions and write answers. However, from an anthropomorphism perspective, this phenomenon is underexplained as to how personal intelligent assistant services can affect consumers' behavioral intention in extant literature. Thus, in order to address this empirical knowledge void, an extensive literature review was undertaken and five hypotheses were derived to explain the potential relationships. Quantitative methodology with a survey strategy was undertaken drawing an effective sample size of 254 Gen-Z consumers. Furthermore, analysis was carried out using Smart partial least squares (PLS)-structural equation modelling. The study first finds a significant direct relationship between the perceived anthropomorphism, perceived enjoyment and perceived trust. Furthermore, perceived enjoyment and perceived trust significantly impact on awe experience and purchase intention among the Gen- Z retail consumers. The findings shed the light on improving customer experience and marketing effectiveness through IPA.

articleTitle: Digital Twins as a Framework for IoT Applications: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The integration of Digital Twins (DT) and Internet of Things (IoT) technologies has emerged with significant advancements across various domains. This review paper explores the fundamentals of Digital Twins, categorizations, state-of-the-art developments, and their integration with IoT. It dives into architectural considerations, data integration, communications, and analytical insights within the concept of using Digital Twins as a framework for IoT applications. Recent advancements, challenges and future directions are also discussed, highlighting the potential and complexities of this combined approach.

articleTitle: Utilizing Ensemble Learning in Detecting Parkinson's Disease with Reduced Facial Expressions and Hand-Written Drawings
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Parkinson's Disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder that affects individuals' movement, planning, initiation, and execution. Some of the most common symptoms of PD are tremors, rigidity, and initiation difficulties. Due to the rigidity in facial muscles, PD patients experience reduced facial expressions also known as Hypomimia. And tremor effects on the PD individual's handwriting abilities. Therefore, these two symptoms can be used in detecting PD in the early stages. The utilization of computer-aided approaches in PD diagnosis has improved worldwide over the last few years. Among these techniques, Machine Learning (ML) models have proven a promising success in PD diagnosis. And it resolves most of the issues such as patients' participation in multiple tests for the diagnosis. In this study, video based facial expression dataset and handwriting drawing dataset are collected from PD diagnosed individuals and non-PD individuals as the input. The accuracy is measured with different algorithms. By applying two-layer stacking ensemble learning framework the predictive accuracy is enhanced. The ensemble makes use of the base models, an attention layer, and a stacking model to combine their predictive strengths. The base models consist of the Logistic Regression method and SVM model.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Indoor Localization System to Support 5G Location-Based Services
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Indoor positioning is expected to play a vital role in future 5G networks, as it enables a wide range of location-based services such as indoor navigation, inventory monitoring, store locators, and anti-theft prevention. Accurate and reliable positioning information is crucial for many 5G applications, and it has been identified as a key enabler by the Third Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), which recently standardized advanced positioning methods in Release 15 and 16. This work focuses on the feasibility of using Machine Learning (ML) algorithms for Long Range Wide Area (LoRa)-based wireless indoor positioning systems, where LoRa-enabled sensor nodes can smoothly access 5G networks. The study trains different ML classifiers, such as Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Gaussian Naïve Basis, on Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) values received from three different anchor nodes in an experimental setup. The experimental results demonstrate that KNN provides over 98% accuracy, 0.9831 precision, 0.9841 recall, and 0.9835 F1 score in estimating the location. This high level of accuracy and reliability makes ML algorithms a promising solution for indoor positioning systems in 5G networks, opening up new opportunities for location-based services such as roadside assistance in indoor scenarios, taxi-hailing, and service locators.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease using Neuro Imaging and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Accurately diagnosing the stages of Alzheimer's disease (AD) using MRI images poses a challenge for medical practitioners, as even experienced professionals can make mistakes in diagnosing the stage. Traditional solutions heavily rely on various MRI pre-processing techniques to improve diagnostic accuracy. In recent years, deep learning methods, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), have shown promise in AD diagnosis through classification approaches. However, there is still a need to bridge the research gap in utilizing deep learning techniques for object detection in Alzheimer's disease diagnosis. In this research, comprehensive comparisons are conducted and various techniques to address this gap are explored, aiming to identify the most effective approach for solving this diagnostic challenge. We introduce hyperparameter tuning in our CNN model to identify the best parameters for achieving optimal accuracy by considering execution time. Next, we compare the accuracy and loss metrics of various CNN architectures' respective execution times. Additionally, we examine the impact of dataset augmentation techniques and the number of data samples on accuracy, loss, and execution times. Our proposed CNN model incorporates the latest techniques, featuring the EfficientNetV2S architecture. Hence, our work provides a benchmark for deep learning-based Alzheimer's disease stage detection, categorizing individuals into four stages Mild Demented, Moderate Demented, Non Demented, and Very Mild Demented. The utilization of the dataset using MRI data from the ADNI, with its extensive 2D slices for each stage, enables the extraction of meaningful features and patterns associated with Alzheimer's disease pathology. The outcomes of this study contribute to the advancement of diagnostic tools and therapeutic interventions, enhancing the understanding and management of Alzheimer's disease.

articleTitle: Utilizing Machine Learning for Forecasting Profitable Vegetable Crops and Land Use in Sri Lankan Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: The agriculture sector faces numerous challenges, such as the selection of profitable vegetable crops, the reduction of surplus vegetable stocks, and the minimization of product losses in various vegetable varieties. This research study aims to address these challenges by employing machine learning to predict the most profitable vegetable crop and the corresponding land area required for cultivation. This anal-ysis considers multiple factors, including weather conditions, cultivation expenses, seasons, location, production data, and historical crop cultivation data. Multiple machine learning algorithms were employed to develop accurate crop prediction models namely, random forest RF, multinomial logistic regression MLR, and Long Short-Term Memory LSTM. The results indicate that multinomial logistic regression archives a higher accuracy of 0.84 for crop prediction and the random forest algorithm gives an accuracy of 0.83. The LSTM model demonstrated an R2score of 0.831. The model outputs the most profitable crop, which serves as input for the land extent prediction system. The application predicts the required land area for selected crops using RFR and LR. RFR gives a higher R2score of 0.956, indicating its superior fit to the data while the LR model achieved an R2score of 0.45. The root mean squared error of the RFR was 23.95 whereas the LR model had 89.29. The findings of this research study provide valuable information like crops and land extent to be cultivated in a particular area to increase productivity. The impact of this work extends to enhancing food security and reducing poverty in Sri Lanka by allowing farmers with the tools and knowledge to make correct decisions at the correct time.

articleTitle: Design a Beach Cleaning Robot Based on AI and Node-RED Interface for Debris Sorting and Monitor the Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Innovative technologies have been created as a result of the growing environmental concerns brought on by coastal pollution and the demand for sustainable beach management solutions. The design and execution of this robot which incorporates cutting-edge sensor technologies for parameter measurement and rubbish sorting, culminating in a user-friendly Node-RED interface, are thoroughly studied in this research paper. The solar-powered beach cleaning robot uses artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms to independently navigate and analyze the beach environment in real time. It has a variety of sensors such as LIDAR, DHT22, GPS, and Load Cell to gauge important factors like humidity, temperature, distance, air quality, and weight of trash. The robot has a method for classifying material that allows it to identify and gather different kinds of trash and sort them as paper, plastic, and organic waste, which helps with beach cleanup. It utilizes solar power as a renewable energy source, reducing its carbon footprint. An integrated Node-RED user interface allows people to obtain real-time data, and display the beach state, facilitating human participation and monitoring. The development process, robot design, sensor integration, AI algorithms, and the Node-RED interface are covered in this paper, along with the system's potential to aid in environmentally responsible beach management.

articleTitle: Deep Rule Visualizer: A Novel Explainable Deep Neural Network Visualization Architecture
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: This paper introduces the Deep Rule Visualizer, an architecture designed to enhance the interpretability of deep neural networks (DNNs). By integrating xDNN model, saliency maps, and IF … THEN rules, the architecture provides users with insights into DNN decision-making. We evaluate the visualizer on benchmark datasets, showcasing its effectiveness in explaining predictions. The user interface displays rule images, regions of interest, and a novel Deep Rule Score (DRS), enabling users to assess prediction reliability. Quantitative evaluation confirms that higher Deep Rule Scores align with correct predictions. The visualizer enhances trust in DNN models, aids error identification, and holds potential across diverse domains.

articleTitle: Ontology Based Machine Learning Approach for Predictive Maintenance of Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: Machine maintenance is crucial in industrial environments for safe and efficient operations. Regular maintenance prevents breakdowns, reduces downtime, and extends machinery lifespan. Currently, reactive and preventive maintenance are commonly practiced. Reactive maintenance repairs machines after failures, leading to unexpected downtime and negative impacts on production. Preventive maintenance follows a predefined schedule to prevent issues, but it can increase costs through inappropriate maintenance and equipment replacements. Predictive maintenance, supported by AI, offers a solution by continuously monitoring machines and predicting faults. This approach minimizes production and maintenance costs, resulting in higher profit margins. This work presents an improved predictive maintenance for industrial machinery based on machine learning and ontology. The objective is to detect patterns in robot health, predict future failures, classify failures, and recommend maintenance tasks. A hybrid maintenance solution is developed, combining ML-based fault prediction with an ontology-based maintenance task recommendation system. The ML model identifies anomalies and patterns for future failure prediction. The ontology model recommends maintenance tasks based on these predictions. The work primarily focuses on the ML-based approach, integrated with the ontology-based approach, to predict machine failures and optimize maintenance strategies, reducing costs and drawbacks of reactive and preventive maintenance.

articleTitle: Identifying Key Aspects of How People Experience Co-creative System: In Reference to Weavesilk Application
publicationTitle: 2023 7th SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of co-creative systems, an intersection of human creativity and artificial intelligence (AI), this research aims to uncover the subjective experiences of individuals engaged in human-AI, human-human, and machine-machine interactions. While co-creative systems have made significant strides, understanding the nuances of user experiences remains an understudied area. This study bridges the gap by systematically exploring the key aspects of user experiences and their influence on the development and efficacy of co-creative systems. The multifaceted nature of co-creative systems enables users to explore, create, and solve problems across domains, such as art, poetry, humor, robotics, and computer games. To grasp the significance of user experiences within these systems, it is imperative to consider diverse modes of interaction human-human collaboration, human-AI engagement, and machine-machine collaboration, each contributing distinct challenges and opportunities to the user experience. A critical research gap emerges when considering the technical capabilities of co-creative systems in comparison to the exploration of user experiences. This research seeks to address this imbalance by delving into the personal narratives of participants who engage with co-creative systems. By employing a qualitative approach and thematic analysis, we reveal invaluable insights into user experiences. The diverse participant pool, representing regions including India, Hong Kong, Nigeria, and Sri Lanka, enriches this exploration by offering a comprehensive understanding of user perspectives. The thematic analysis uncovers recurring themes that encapsulate the dimensions of user experiences, covering both positive and negative aspects. Key themes include the sharing of workloads on tasks, the systematic navigation of steps in the creative process, and the mechanics of user interaction with the system. These insights bridge the divide between theoretical research and practical application, offering actionable implications for the development of more user-centric co-creative systems. This research holds significant relevance to the conference, as it addresses pivotal questions in the co-creative systems domain and contributes to the ongoing discourse on the role of these systems in fostering human-AI collaboration and driving innovation across various domains. Focusing on user experiences paves the way for co-creative systems that are not only technically advanced but also engaging and transformative.
